VBO:0008093.summary: Described by a keeper as soft-spirited and fond of attention, the South African Greyhound often joins daily runs or brisk walks. Also called the Boerwindhond, it is a working hunting cross shaped by farmers, with individuals and lines varying. Its work includes pack coursing and pursuing livestock predators such as jackals and caracals.
VBO:0008093.shortDescription: A variable South African working cross, with a history of pack coursing and a keeper’s reports of soft-spirited company.

sources.title: De Jager Kennels: firsthand Boerwindhond keeper account
sources.evidence: Actual complete keeper text describes love of attention, sociability and soft-spirited dogs, daily run/intensive walk, farmer jackal/predator hunting, varied crosses in different lines. Own bitches said registered with SABWV and offspring judged at minimum one year; not independently verified registry or all photographed dogs. Health/lifespan/superior stamina/intelligence/weather/pain/guarding/child suitability guarantees excluded. Adult photos under own dogs and Boerwindhonde labels personally viewed whole; explicit puppy/young images excluded.

sources.title: Africanis Society: AfriCanis and the distinct greyhound-type working cross
sources.evidence: Actual full article explicitly distinguishes AfriCanis landrace from purposefully crossed African Greyhound/Boerwindhond working type, pack hunting/coursing, sheep farmers hunting caracal/jackal. Literal type anatomy: elongated head, deep narrow chest, arched back, low-set hanging tail, angular rear legs. Ancestry lists not inherited behavior/morphology. Article minimum75cm not universal imposed on keeper females65cm. Township dogs and illegal-hunt criticism excluded from product copy.

VBO:0200349.summary: Alert and energetic, the Chinese Foo Dog is bred for a dignified, independent character and loyalty to its household. Hunting and watchdog work feature in its breed tradition. Swiss and Austrian breeding has sustained a small European population, with pedigree research shaped by a dwindling pool of breeding females.
VBO:0200349.shortDescription: An alert, energetic spitz with an independent streak, bred for household loyalty alongside hunting and watchdog work.

sources.title: Chinese Foo Dog — attributed club standard on keeper website
sources.evidence: Personally read entire German standard: active/agile/alert/energetic, dignified independent nature and loyal family member; hunting/working roots and friendly competent watchdog breeding ideal. Complete square spitz anatomy, wedge head, natural erect/semi-erect ears, four limb/paw clauses, intact high tail over back, double coat and permitted orange/red color. Breeding ideal is calibrated as bred-for, not established individual behavior prevalence.

sources.title: Chinese Foo Dog — Austrian keepers’ own breeding and pedigree history
sources.evidence: Actual entire home body names Swiss-born Bonny October2014/deceasedJanuary2022, own Austrian litters August2016 andNovember2019; Ayka/Bolt/Boomer remain in household per keeper account. Describes Swiss litters and pedigree/mating investigations, shortage of breeding females. Historical counts through2023 explicitly uncertain because deaths are not universally reported; no current2026 census asserted.

sources.title: Chinese Foo Dog — keeper breeding-plan statement
sources.evidence: Whole actual planning body states no further European breeding possibilities owing to small population and unsuccessful search abroad. Explicitly limits inference from maintained living dogs: no current active breeding or viable long-term future guaranteed.
